summary: A humorous, satirical essay casting e-commerce versus local retailers as a battle, with shopkeeper Localized Lady (Linda Smith) trying weak discounts and gimmicks against online giants. It mocks the decline of in-person interaction, the discount culture, and slow delivery, and ends with local shops trying artisanal workshops and a speculative future of drones.
one_line: A satirical take on local retailers struggling against e-commerce through discounts, workshops, and nostalgia for in-person shopping.
key_facts: A September 2023 local survey by pollster Dr. Click N. Buy claimed 89% of the population prefers shopping in pajamas over leaving the house.
Dr. Click N. Buy said, "The trend towards digital consumerism is unstoppable," comparing it to athleisure wear and kale smoothies.
The essay jokes that the volume of e-commerce packaging led to a fitness trend called 'Boxercise.'
Localized Lady, whose real name is Linda Smith, is the archetype of the small business owner who runs a boutique.
On October 12, Linda Smith held up a sign reading "If you can find it online, you can buy it for 10% more here!", which was not a success.
Jones, a cashier at 'Everything's a Dollar More Here' store, said on November 5 that he misses when 'checking out' meant more than a quick swipe or tap.
On Black Friday, Localized Lady ran 'Moderate Markdown Madness' with discounts of up to 10%, which online customers found quaint.
On December 3, delivery driver Terry Quickship said people are surprised when he drops off a package a week after they forgot they ordered it.
Some local shops respond with artisanal experiences and handmade goods, such as workshops like "Make Your Own Candle and Then Burn It" and "Vegan Taxidermy: An Oxymoron?"
The essay suggests that a small business victory, if it comes, could be Pyrrhic.
It speculates that drones may darken the skies, bringing immediate gratification full circle.
Notifications from MegaSave.com are used as a symbol of the decline of conversation in commerce.
